PR #70, "Build cache in the registry; pull requests from collaborators only" (branch `build-cache-in-registry` into `main`). It adds a per-architecture build cache in GHCR and drops fork handling from the workflow.

**`.github/workflows/images.yml`**
- `PUBLISH` and the `publish` job's `if` no longer check whether the pull request comes from this repository. The condition is now `pull_request || ref == main`.
- The "Log in to GHCR" step runs unconditionally, because every run now reads and writes the cache.
- The bake step sets `CACHE: true`.

**`images/docker-bake.hcl`**
- New `CACHE` variable (default false) and the helpers `cache_ref`, `cache_from` and `cache_to`.
- The cache ref is `${REGISTRY}/<image>:cache-<arch>`, with the arch taken from `PLATFORM`.
- The export uses `mode=max,image-manifest=true,oci-mediatypes=true`.
- All four targets (`core`, `core-systemd`, `coder-template`, `devcontainer-base`) get `cache-from` and `cache-to`. The rest of the diff in this file is alignment whitespace.

**`README.md`**
- Says the `cache-amd64` and `cache-arm64` tags are CI's build cache and are not images to pull.
- Adds a paragraph saying the repository takes no outside contributions and does not support forks, linking ADR 0020.

**`docs/adr/0020-pull-requests-from-collaborators-only.md`** (new)
- Records that pull requests come only from collaborators' branches and Renovate, and that a fork pull request fails its checks.
- Lists the old fork behaviour (build and test without publishing) and a reduced fork path per feature as considered options.

**`docs/adr/0021-build-cache-in-the-registry.md`** (new)
- Records the decision: every CI run reads and writes a per-architecture cache in each image's own GHCR package, and local builds do not use it.
- Considered options: no cache, the GitHub Actions cache, and a separate cache package per image.
- Consequences: the cache tags are visible in the package, superseded cache versions stay as untagged versions, and pull requests and `main` share one cache and overwrite each other's.

- 58 and 60 steps came from the cache on the second run.

I found no high-signal problems in PR #70. I only reviewed the changed code, and I could only read files: shell access was denied, so I didn't run bake or the workflow.

The points you asked me to check:

- **When it publishes:** The workflow runs on `pull_request`, on `push` to `main`, and on `workflow_dispatch`. It has no `schedule` or `merge_group` trigger.
  - A push to `main` publishes.
  - A manual run on `main` publishes.
  - A manual run on any other branch does not publish, so `edge` doesn't move.
  - A pull request publishes `pr-N`.

  Apart from dropping the fork check, the new `PUBLISH` expression and the publish job's `if` give the same results as the old ones. Fork pull requests will now fail at the GHCR login or the push, which matches the PR description and ADR 0020.
- **The cache flag and `PLATFORM`:** CI only sets `CACHE=true` in the `build` job, and every matrix leg sets `PLATFORM: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}`. So the cache tag is always `cache-amd64` or `cache-arm64`. Local builds leave `CACHE` off and get no cache settings, so an empty `PLATFORM` never produces a broken `cache-` tag. `CACHE=true` arrives from the environment as a string, and the existing `PUSH` variable already relies on bake reading it that way.
- **Permissions:** The `build` job already has `packages: write`, and the GHCR login now always runs, so every run can write the cache.
- **The bake functions:** `replace` is a standard bake HCL function. Calling one user function from another already works in this file (`out` calls `img`). The `cache-from` and `cache-to` values are valid lists of strings. On the first run the cache tag doesn't exist yet; bake only warns about that and doesn't fail.
- **Cleanup:** `.github/workflows/ghcr-cleanup.yml` only deletes stale `pr-N` tags and keeps untagged versions, so it never deletes the `cache-*` tags. That matches what ADR 0021 says.

Following AGENTS.md: I set aside one finding. PR and `main` runs write to the same per-architecture cache, so each overwrites the other's. ADR 0021 already accepts this, so I didn't report it.
